_comment: Release criteria of Phase 1 (roadmap.md 'Shared release criteria' and 'Phase 1 - Measurable exit criteria', technical-decisions.md 10.2). evidence = ["CHECK-ID@artifact"]: the named check of the named evidence artifact must be PASS and the artifact must have a computed SHA-256. A criterion with no evidence, a missing result or a skipped target is UNVERIFIED.

criteria.text: A fresh installation from the repository's documented Compose file starts, passes health/readiness and completes the Phase 1 end-to-end scenarios (clean Compose deployment with containers A/B and a real MCP client).

Image size budget: compressed production image <= 60 MB (10^6 bytes), measured on each CPU: from the real gzip OCI export where the daemon can produce one (the VM), otherwise from a documented docker-save estimate (the hosted runners).

Idle resource budget (technical-decisions.md 10.2 as clarified): resident set <= 50 MB after stabilization, measured over the final 60 s of a 300 s observation window after readiness, with SQLite initialized and one local Docker endpoint connected (after first start, after configuration and after a restart; the maximum of the samples in the window is gated). The start-up memory peak and the time to stabilization are reported separately; the idle limit does not apply to that start-up transient.
criteria.limits: Measured on one amd64 host (4 CPUs); the arm64 figure is the hosted-runner run, not a calibrated host.

criteria.text: Load resource budget: resident set <= 150 MB under the approved workload (10 REST + 10 real-MCP polling clients and 5 follow streams), peak reset at the start of the window.
criteria.limits: The workload is the one defined in docs/release-acceptance.md; it is a footprint workload, not a throughput claim.

criteria.text: The service keeps authorizing legitimate calls under the approved workload (no spurious fail-closed refusal of a granted call while 20 clients and 5 streams are active).

adverse.disposition: OWNER-APPROVED DISPOSITION (section 6, R2 / SH-2d; reviewer run 518 option 1): the adverse runs stay FAIL as recorded and are not rewritten. The cause is established (daemon saturation amplified by the service's own continuity reads) and the bounded continuity cache removes most of that amplification (docs/release-acceptance.md, R2 measurement: clean 10+10 all targets met; contended REL-LOAD-STABLE failed in 15/15 A runs and passed in 30/30 B runs; 669 against 0 timeouts, 191 against 0 refusals), but the pre-registered drop-rate statistic is NOT met (2/15 against 0/30 runs with a drop, one-sided Fisher p = 0.106, target p < 0.05) and the original clean-host failures were not exactly reproduced. The owner accepted this evidence as the disposition of R2: this is an acceptance-policy decision, not a pass of the statistic, and it waives nothing in security. Residual risk: a fail-closed availability refusal under a saturated daemon.

criteria.limits: Not a named budget: it is the precondition for the load figure to describe a working service, so it is recorded as its own criterion and never folded into the memory result.

criteria.text: The documented local development workflow runs the application and unit tests without building or running a container.
CI runs unit tests, integration/security regression tests and build checks non-interactively; every required check passed for the release artifact (the code commit of this release).
criteria.limits: The hosted run is the one on the code commit that precedes the evidence commit; CI on the evidence commit is part of the reviewer's exact-head check.

criteria.text: Every exposed operation has positive and negative authorization tests through each applicable interface (REST and MCP); omitting a tool is not enforcement; revoked and expired credentials and permissions fail.

Security review covers the changed attack surface; no unresolved release-blocking High/Critical finding: Go and frontend static analysis and advisory scans, reachable-vulnerability scan, image scan and SBOM.
criteria.limits: The independent reviewer's verdict on the exact head is recorded on the Kanban card and the PR, not in this file; a scanner finding or a scanner failure is a failure, never an exception.

criteria.text: Policy and usage persistence survives a graceful restart and a SIGKILL crash.

A backup is restored into a fresh instance (full same-key and clean new-key), compared against the documented scope, quarantined until a host-authorized recovery and explicit approval, and the restored instance passes authorization tests.

Upgrade/data migration preserves the supported prior-version data (real populated store lowered to the prior schema with the repository's own down-migration, then upgraded by the release image); a newer store is refused; the guarded downgrade is refused.
Application-wide logging honors MANDATARY_LOG_LEVEL; no password, token, TOTP seed, master key, address proof or session cookie appears in any log of any deployment of the run or in any archive.
Shipped web interfaces work in both light and dark mode, in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, on desktop and a 390x844 phone viewport, with WebAuthn on a virtual authenticator.
criteria.limits: Browser suites ran on the coder's controller host against the exact commit, not through the TLS proxy of the Compose deployment (no real browser through the proxy).

criteria.text: Operator documentation, configuration examples, supported-version policy and known limitations match the delivered release (mechanical checks; accuracy of prose is a reviewer judgment).
Acceptance results are recorded against a versioned release artifact (exact commit, image digest and binary digest); undelivered later-phase features are unavailable, not insecure stubs.
From a clean Compose deployment: bootstrap an administrator, create a user/group and agent identity, grant a function on test container A, and call it through both the API and a real MCP client.

Denials for an unauthenticated caller, a second ungranted function, test container B and each unsupported operation; policy/credential revocation; no alternate forwarding bypass (no daemon event on B, on Mandatary itself or on its labelled peer).
Password-policy, TOTP enrollment/verification/recovery, brute-force controls, session expiry and the phishing-resistant authenticator pass the Step 0 security scenarios.
criteria.limits: These scenarios are the Go suites of internal/auth (mapped to NIST-ID rows in docs/*.md) and the browser suites; this report links their suite-level results, and the setup/recovery steps of the release run, not each scenario.

criteria.text: A restart preserves policies and usage counts; backup/restore into a fresh instance reproduces the defined settings and the correct allow/deny behaviour.

A predetermined sequence of operations produces exactly the expected user/container/function counts under the agreed counting rules (every executed matrix, lifecycle and workload outcome is accounted per agent, owner, selector and operation).
Both CPU architectures: the release image deploys, passes the matrix and meets the image budget on linux/amd64 and linux/arm64.
criteria.limits: arm64 runs only on the hosted arm64 runner (operator-approved); no arm64 VM was available.
